question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5
solution:
The correct answer is '**together**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage emphasizes the role of the press in bridging the gap between the government and the people.
 
• The term chosen should reflect the idea of uniting or bringing both the rulers and the ruled into closer communication.
 
• "**Together**" is appropriate as it indicates the act of uniting the government and the people, aligning with the context of the passage.
 
• Other options ("**apart**", "**overall**", "**jointed**") do not fit because they do not convey the idea of uniting both parties.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The newspaper is one of the significant signs of modern civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the present times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us both entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. No government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled together.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Apart (अलग): "Apart" means separated by a distance, which is the opposite of the context intended in the passage.
 
• Overall (कुल मिलाकर): "Overall" is used to indicate generalization, which does not fit the context of uniting two entities.
 
• Jointed (संयुक्त): "Jointed" means having connections, typically in a structured form, but it does not fit grammatically or contextually in the sentence.
